_about: written judgement about what each model is for. SOURCE, not derived: analyze-usecase
carries it into data/usecase.json beside the numbers, and never overwrites it.
the numbers lead. every `evidence` entry names a facet and the percentile the model
holds on it WITHIN this registry -- p79 means it beat 79% of the registry models that
carry the same facet, not 79% of every model in the world. `claim` marks a number the
model published about itself, which analyze-self-report measures as running about +0.9
high, and which is the weakest evidence here.
confidence is about the EVIDENCE, not the model: high means several independent
third-party sources agree, medium means one source or a thin sample, low means nobody
has measured it and this is the card plus whatever the forums said.
WHO WROTE EACH BLOCK is not here. it was, as `author` and `authored_against`,
until four other surfaces needed the same record and had nowhere to put it --
a yaml `note:` is a string and an html attribute is an attribute. one ledger
holds it for all five now: research/prose.json, keyed `usecase:<repo>`. see
research/prose.py for the inventory and ./write-prose for the door into it.

Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.one_liner: the strongest dense model in the registry on measured axes, and the current default answer for a single 27b that has to do everything.
Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B.notes: gbench has not played it yet, so its evidence is aa plus its own card plus 304 reddit mentions at 90% approval. the template defaults thinking to xhigh, which costs 15k-52k thinking tokens in reported traces against qwen3.6's 3k. it is also the value pick: the top score out of the smallest file of anything near it, which leaves most of a 128gb box free for context or a second model. one reproducible benchmark on this exact silicon reports UD-Q5_K_XL at 16.68 t/s against Q8_0's 12.74, with MTP at 4 draft tokens under vulkan -- one reporter on one box, so a reason to test the lower quant rather than a recommendation to run it.

Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.one_liner: the qwen4 architecture preview, among the highest-measured models here -- bought with a 51b n-gram table that is most of what makes it awkward to serve.
Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.notes: artificial analysis scored it three days after release, and it leads qwen3.8-27b on most of the axes the two share: {aa.intelligence:value} against {aa.intelligence@Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B:value}, terminal-bench {aa.terminalbench:value} against {aa.terminalbench@Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B:value}. three go the other way and they are the ones to know about: the 27b answers where this one declines ({aa.non_hallucination} against {aa.non_hallucination@Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B}), holds a longer context better ({aa.lcr} against {aa.lcr@Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B}) and is ahead on tool use ({aa.tau_banking} against {aa.tau_banking@Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B}). what the forums discuss is none of that. {community.hf-discussions}, almost all about speed and memory: "~ 11ts (no MTP)" {q:92272aaa} against a 22 for qwen3.5 122b on the same box. the main ggufs carry no MTP head, and the separate heads unsloth has since published need llama.cpp PR 28243, still open, so a stock build decodes without one. 41% of the file is the n-gram table, which is what both the '4x slower than it should be' and the 'keep the n-gram table on nvme' threads are about, and it is also why the quant ladder bottoms out at 67.6gib -- its 160-column rows take only block-32 types. AtomicChat is the one publisher that shards the table separately, so 38 of their 93 gb page from ssd rather than staying resident.
evidence: {community.hf-discussions}, reddit 85 mentions at 100% approval on two scored posts

deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731.one_liner: the registry's strongest all-rounder: top decile on science, coding, long context and physics at once, and the most discussed model after qwen3.6.
deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731.notes: at UD-IQ3_XXS it is 97gib, so on a 128gb box it fits with a drafter and little else. best go play measured here at 82%. v4's compressed sparse attention makes the kv cache far cheaper than a generic reserve assumes -- deepseek reports the 1m setting costing 27% of what the naive form would -- which is what leaves room for the 10.2gib dspark drafter beside it. two complaints from people actually running it: it ignores rules files and skill definitions, which the thread attributes to deepseek shipping no official jinja template and each quant publisher writing their own, so pin a known-good template rather than trusting the gguf default; and where the fitting quant is too tight, the community's answer for this class of box is Rednalreden's dwarfstar, a single 80.8gib file that keeps Q8 attention projections, shared experts and output layer while dropping the routed experts to IQ2_XXS.

deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813.notes: the best-measured model added this sweep -- aa, gbench, lmarena, swe-rebench and its own card all carry it -- and the one clear weakness is non-hallucination, {aa.non_hallucination}: it answers rather than declines, which is the opposite of minimax m3 beside it. the language breakdown is lopsided: {lang.csharp}, {lang.rust} and {lang.kotlin} against {lang.javascript} and {lang.typescript}. one reddit comment says "new testing has come out to suggest that Deepseek V4 Pro August is benchmaxxed" {q:50251580}; that is a claim rather than a measurement, and five agreeing sources are what it would have to overturn.

deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.one_liner: a 552b multimodal moe whose whole argument is the kv cache -- 890 bytes a token, a quarter of v4 flash -- and which nothing on this roster can currently run.
use_for: tracking what the roster cannot currently load
avoid_for: work where declining to answer beats a confident guess
deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.notes: released 2026-09-10, and the third parties have caught up since: artificial analysis puts it at {aa.intelligence}, with {aa.lcr} on long context and {aa.terminalbench_v40} on terminal work, and gbench at {gbench.overall}. the axis it falls off is declining to answer, {aa.non_hallucination}: it answers where it should not. what the card claims is worth watching for this roster specifically: the global kv cache is 890 bytes per token against v4 flash's ~3.5kib, which is the number that decides whether a 1m context is affordable rather than nominal, and only 8b of 552b is active in prefill. the checkpoint also takes images, which v4 flash did not. the practical position is the opposite of the scores. apetersson's 157gib mixed-q2 is uncalibrated and missing the engram tables, the dspark blocks and the vision tensors, and its own publisher records that no runtime has executed it end to end. the conventional k-quant ladder is vcruz305's, whole now from Q2_K up, and its card says the files do not run on upstream llama.cpp yet: the converter is an open PR, and the runtime is a branch of vcruz305's own fork with sparse attention still the unfinished piece. treat the card facets here with more than the usual suspicion: the extractor read the BASE model table, so `card.gpqa` is the 53.1 of supergpqa rather than the 90.9 the instruct model claims on gpqa diamond.
evidence: vcruz305's ladder runs on its own llama.cpp branch, not upstream

meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B.one_liner: the best long-context reader in the registry, and a strong game player, with an operational reputation problem.
meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B.notes: aa long-context reasoning {aa.lcr} and gbench {gbench.overall}, against {community.hf-discussions} and {community.reddit-localllama}. read the discussion tab before committing: that pattern is usually a quant that does not load rather than a model that cannot think, and reddit leaning the other way is what makes the loading reading the likelier one.

microsoft/Fara1.5-27B.one_liner: a browser agent that sees only screenshots: it is unranked here because the three suites it reports are carried by no source in this corpus.
use_for: browser automation and web tasks under microsoft's own harness
screenshot-grounded ui work, where pixel coordinates are the output
avoid_for: any harness other than the fara cli or magentic-ui
microsoft/Fara1.5-27B.notes: unranked rather than bad, the same as qwen-agentworld: webvoyager, online-mind2web and webtailbench are web-agent suites, and aa, gbench, lmarena, swe-rebench and epoch carry none of them. what the card does show is a clean size ladder across its own family -- webvoyager 80.8 at 4b, 86.6 at 9b, 89.3 at 27b -- which is the shape of a real capability gain rather than a cherry-picked number. it is a supervised fine-tune of qwen3.5-27b, already carried here, so the honest comparison is against that base and nothing measures the delta. the mmproj sidecar is required, not optional: screenshots are the entire input.
evidence: no facet carried by any source
card webvoyager 89.3 claim, against 86.6 at 9b and 80.8 at 4b

mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B.one_liner: a fast dense 128b that calls tools well and does no science at all.
mistralai/Mistral-Medium-3.5-128B.notes: critpt {aa.critpt} twice over, from both aa and epoch, is a consistent verdict rather than one bad run. perfect javascript play over the games it was given.

mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602.one_liner: realtime multilingual speech transcription whose card claims offline-grade accuracy, and whose open asr score does not bear that out.
mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602.notes: the card says that at a 480ms delay it matches leading offline open-source transcribers, and the open asr board, which ranks offline open transcribers, puts it at {open-asr.accuracy}. it also gives up a control the batch mini has: "voxtral realtime doesn't support any language hints like voxtral mini does" {q:65e054b8}.
evidence: card: realtime, multilingual, accuracy comparable to offline open models at 480ms

moonshotai/Kimi-K3.one_liner: the most capable model in this registry on every reasoning axis, and at 553gib the one that costs the most to find that out.
avoid_for: anything that has to fit in 128gb
moonshotai/Kimi-K3.notes: the top of the registry on six axes at once. its thinking knob is `thinking_effort`, whose guard rejects the `medium` its own injected prose says it supports. decode is {aa.speed}, the second slowest here.

nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF.one_liner: fast and good at contest maths on its own card, weak on everything a third party measured.
nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF.notes: {card.aime:value} is its own claim; the third-party numbers around it sit far lower, {aa.lcr} on long context and {aa.terminalbench_hard} on agentic software work. the gap between claim and measurement is the story of this entry. the conversions add to it: one tester found "the `Q4_K_M`quant wouldn't load" {q:18347fc1}, and another that the throughput is not what was promised, "the results aren't matching what's advertised" {q:b6b1712b}.

nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B.one_liner: a physics-leaning 120b that only artificial analysis has measured.
nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B.notes: no gbench suite carries it, so {aa.critpt} is most of what is known. its card recommends temp 1.0 across every task including tool calling, and the registry runs it colder anyway -- `upstream-tool-use` records what the vendor actually said.

nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B.one_liner: the fastest model in the registry by a wide margin, and it spends all of that speed being average.
nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B.notes: {aa.speed:value} with intelligence at {aa.intelligence}. worth it when volume matters more than the answer; not otherwise. read the low rungs before picking one: "On Nemotron-3.5-Lightning all four IQ2 rungs are the same 4.58 bpw file under four different names" {q:7086c554}.

openai/gpt-oss-120b.one_liner: fast, widely run, and beaten on quality by most of what it sits beside -- but the best pure language play measured here.
openai/gpt-oss-120b.notes: 100% gbench success in go, c++ and java against aa coding and agentic near the bottom, and no arena rating at all. it compiles what it is asked for and loses the argument about what to ask for.

openai/gpt-oss-20b.one_liner: the small gpt-oss: quick, cheap, and out of its depth on anything agentic.

openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo.one_liner: the pruned whisper large v3: the most widely deployed open asr, faster than the model it came from rather than more accurate.
avoid_for: english-only work where a newer transcriber scores higher
openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo.notes: {open-asr.accuracy} and {aa-stt.accuracy}, so it is the default for reach rather than for accuracy. the distil-whisper maintainers still point multilingual users at it: "For multilingual use cases, I'd recommend openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo or other recent models from HF Open ASR Leaderboard" {q:601adda9}. it shares large-v3's habit of inventing words, reported for both: "I am very certain that my audios don't contain these words" {q:58a88caf}.
evidence: card: state of the art asr and speech translation

poolside/Laguna-S-2.1.one_liner: the middle laguna, and the one the forums actually run, with no benchmark in this corpus left to check them against.
use_for: agentic work on a community-fixed template
avoid_for: agentic work on the stock template
poolside/Laguna-S-2.1.notes: no board carries it, so the forums are the evidence, and they are warm: {community.hf-discussions} and {community.reddit-localllama}. people run it for code -- "Still using Laguna S 2.1 a lot for pure coding" {q:a3d8b9b5} -- and for agents only after a template fix, which one user credits with making it "genuinely usable for me: it's now driving both a local agent (Hermes) and a coding lane on an all-Mac fleet, where before it wandered" {q:21c1fdc2}. the fix combines qwen template corrections with laguna's own, so use it rather than the template the weights ship.
evidence: no gbench, aa, lmarena, swe-rebench or epoch facet

poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1.one_liner: a fifth of the s's size that beats it on ten of their sixteen shared facets, and on javascript by 68 points.
use_for: one-shot coding where 19 gib is the whole budget
avoid_for: python and kotlin, where the s is much better
poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1.notes: {lang.javascript} against the s's is the largest same-family inversion in the registry, and it holds on typescript and java too; python and kotlin go the other way by as much. it inherits the family's flaw undiluted -- {gbench.agentic}, one-shot {gbench.oneshot} -- so it is a language model in the literal sense rather than an agent. the vendor publishes the only gguf and it has two rungs, q4_k_m and bf16, so there is no ladder to trade down.

poolside/Laguna-M.1.one_liner: the laguna that trades one-shot coding for agentic work, and sits near the bottom of the gbench board at both.
use_for: agentic / tool use, within the family
avoid_for: anything where a first-tier gguf matters
poolside/Laguna-M.1.notes: gbench {gbench.agentic} where laguna s 2.1 sits at the floor, and one-shot {gbench.oneshot} where the s is far above it: the two sizes have swapped which half of the job they do. against that it is bottom-band on everything else despite being the largest model in the family, and three sources agree on that rather than one. no vendor or first-tier gguf exists -- the single uploader's repo is the only one, though it publishes a 28-point perplexity ladder with it, which is the richest quant sweep in this document.
evidence: scored by gbench, lmarena and epoch

prism-ml/Bonsai-27B-unpacked.one_liner: 27b-class reasoning in binary weights: an efficiency experiment the two forums carrying it disagree about.
prism-ml/Bonsai-27B-unpacked.notes: {community.hf-discussions} against {community.reddit-localllama}. no benchmark carries it, so the reception IS the evidence -- and the two halves of that evidence point opposite ways, which is a weaker claim than this entry used to make. the discussion tab is people failing to load a file -- "failed to load draft model, 'Bonsai-27B-dspark-Q4_1.gguf'" {q:e3d22f68} is typical -- and reddit is people describing what the file does when it loads: it is "just Qwen 3.6 27b quantized with QAT to 1 bit, and it's better than most Q2 or Q3 quants" {q:de2440f8} in one account. neither is a measurement. quantization-aware training to one bit is what it exists to demonstrate, so the bits-per-weight retention curve does not model it and the entry carries native_low_bpw.
evidence: no facet carried by any source

prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-unpacked.one_liner: the ternary sibling of bonsai, with the same reception and the same absence of measurement.
prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-unpacked.notes: {community.hf-discussions}, and the threads are mostly about getting the file to behave. the one to fetch is named in them -- "Ternary-Bonsai-27B-Q2_0.gguf is the correct one to use right now" {q:b27dc96a} -- and the looping and broken tool calls people report go away with the cache left alone: "dont select kv cache q4 or q8, set it as default f16, looping is gone and tool calling works perfect" {q:086fb7f6}. on language work the one test found it "largely unusable" {q:600fe584} for russian rewriting. ternary weights are outside the quantization curve this repo fits, so a bpw comparison against it is meaningless.
evidence: no facet carried by any source

prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf.one_liner: the ternary line's second generation, and the first of them to publish a benchmark table instead of a claim.
use_for: a 27b that runs on one consumer card
avoid_for: anything on a stock llama.cpp build
work where the numbers have to be somebody else's
prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-gguf.notes: released two days before this assessment, so no board scores it and no forum has said anything yet: the whole of the evidence is the vendor's own table, which is the thing the 1.0 entries did not have at all. it reports 84.78 against the fp16 base's 86.32 over fourteen benchmarks, and the useful part is the comparison arms rather than the headline -- their IQ2_XXS build of the same base holds 88.93 on mmlu-redux while falling to 57.5 on aime26, which is the clearest published statement of why a low-bit model can test fine and reason badly. treat the score as a vendor claim: it is measured on their own harness and this repo discounts a card's numbers by about a point for that. what is NOT a claim is the runtime requirement, and it is the reason to be careful -- the card says a stock build takes the Q2_0 file "without any warning" and produces garbage, so the failure mode here is silent output rather than a refusal to load.
evidence: vendor-reported only: no third-party suite carries it
no forum mentions in this corpus

prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-8B-unpacked.one_liner: an 8b that fits in 2 gib of ternary weights, and whose published accuracy a discussion thread says did not reproduce.
use_for: a text model where 2 gib is the entire memory budget
avoid_for: a stock llama.cpp -- the 2 gib q2_0 needs prism-ml's own fork, and the rung that does load is f16 at 15.3 gib
long context, since the 64k window is yarn factor 4.0 over a 16k trained one
anything wanting reasoning -- the shipped template closes the think block unconditionally
prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-8B-unpacked.notes: the card's own table puts it second of six 6-9b models at 1/8th the size, which is the whole claim, and it is a self-run comparison. the only independent signal in this corpus contradicts it -- the top discussion thread on the gguf repo is titled that the reported accuracy could not be replicated, with a user reporting it lagging similar-sized models in lm studio. the compression is real and interesting; the accuracy behind it is not established here.
evidence: {community.hf-discussions} of 33 -- 2 mentions, the thread titled that the reported accuracy could not be replicated
no benchmark facet carried by any source
claim: avg 75.5 against qwen3-8b's 79.3 over six 6-9b models, the vendor's own evalscope run
context_native 65536 is yarn factor 4.0 over a context_trained of 16384

stepfun-ai/Step-3.7-Flash.one_liner: the most reliable tool-caller measured here, and a capable planner, that cannot write a program in one go.
stepfun-ai/Step-3.7-Flash.notes: {aa.tau2:value} with gbench one-shot coding at {gbench.oneshot} is the mirror image of gemma 4 26b. give it tools and steps, not a blank file.

tencent/Hy3.one_liner: top-decile on reasoning and the best-rated model here by human preference, with a gbench sample too thin to quote.
tencent/Hy3.notes: gbench has played it 7 games over 25 matches, which is why its gscore is marked thin rather than used. 49 reddit mentions at 93% approval is the best reception in the registry. the ranking and the people running it disagree, and the disagreement is worth more than either. a handful on 128gb machines rate it first for coding -- "significantly better coder than deepseek-v4-flash, keep using deepseek-v4-flash only if speed is the primary concern" -- against a similar number who found it slow. both can be true: AA measures the unquantized model, the retention curve is transferred from another architecture, and 21b active is more compute per token than anything else that fits. what people report costing them is context and speed rather than quality, roughly 190k against deepseek's 1m, with throughput that drops off brutally as context grows.

thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small.one_liner: a science and physics specialist: {aa.critpt} on critpt, omniscience and scicode at once.
thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small.notes: do not read the flagship inkling's gbench score onto this model -- the generated tables did exactly that once. it is not on the gbench board at all. it is not a chat model either: lmarena puts it at {lmarena.rating}. the {community.hf-discussions} figure is the lexicon misreading the threads, which are warm -- "Thanks very much for the inkling-small release, it's amazing" {q:3092983b} -- and ARC Prize calls it "the highest-scoring open-weight model evaluated by ARC Prize" {q:fe1081e1}.

thinkingmachines/Inkling.one_liner: the flagship the small is small relative to, and it is ahead on only eleven of the twenty-nine facets they share.
avoid_for: running locally at any published rung
formal proof work, where the small beats it outright
thinkingmachines/Inkling.notes: the reason to carry it was to find out what inkling small gives up, and the answer is: knowledge and human preference, not reasoning. it wins simpleqa by 43 points, lmarena by 47 and long-context recall by 17, and it LOSES proofbench by 31 and aime by 21 to a model a fraction of its size. {aa.omniscience} with {aa.omniscience_index} says it knows more and does not pay for it in hallucination, which is the clearest case for the extra weight. read those scores at the setting they were run at: the headline benchmarks are "all reported at `effort = 0.99`, which measures the model under a full internal scratchpad" {q:c7b76ec2}. nothing about that is runnable here -- bf16 is 1.76 tib and the smallest rung is 252 gib, so this is a reference point like kimi k3.
evidence: scored by aa, gbench, lmarena and epoch

upstage/Solar-Open2-250B.one_liner: an office-and-document moe whose strongest measured axis is declining to make things up, with physics close behind.
upstage/Solar-Open2-250B.notes: {aa.non_hallucination} and {aa.critpt} are its two highest, well above {aa.intelligence}. the one sustained forum report is a blind-comparison series whose second instalment cooled on the first -- it "remained competitive, but the expanded data is less dramatic than the first three-day snapshot suggested" {q:1e953ff5}. running it locally "needs a patch on llama cpp and then a build" {q:e646546b}. its template collapses medium, high and xhigh into one branch, so the thinking knob has one effective setting under three names, and the `none` its card documents changes nothing at all.

yuxinlu1/gemma-4-12B-agentic-fable5-comp.one_liner: the same 12b continued into tool use, carrying one agentic number that its own author ran.
use_for: local coding and terminal agent loops at 12b
a tool-calling model that fits an 8 gib card at q3_k_m
avoid_for: customer-service style agents -- the card puts the base model AHEAD of it on tau2 retail
general knowledge, which its own card puts below the base
any comparison against published tau2-bench figures
yuxinlu1/gemma-4-12B-agentic-fable5-comp.notes: the headline is ~55% on tau2-bench telecom against the base model's ~15%, and the card is unusually honest about what that is -- the author's own harness, 20 tasks, a self-simulated user, all at q8_0, which measures v2 against its base under one setup and nothing else. the forum signal points the other way, since every agentic-task mention it has is neutral or negative. needs --jinja for the native tool format and rep_pen 1.1 to avoid a repetition failure, so a bad first impression here is usually the client.
evidence: {community.hf-discussions} of 33 -- 7 mentions over 4 threads, 2 negative and 0 positive
6 agentic-task mentions in hf-discussions, 2 negative and 0 positive
no benchmark facet carried by any source
claim: tau2-bench telecom ~55% against the base's ~15%, author's own harness over 20 tasks
claim: mmlu-pro below the base model, also the author's own run

yuxinlu1/gemma-4-12B-coder-fable5-compos.one_liner: a 12b python coder whose only measurement is its own card, and whose author has already superseded it.
use_for: python and algorithmic coding on a small card
a private coding assistant where q4_k_m at 6.9 gib is the whole budget
avoid_for: general knowledge, which the card says is what was traded away
tool use and agent loops -- that is what v2 was built to fix
any slot that needs a third-party number to justify it
yuxinlu1/gemma-4-12B-coder-fable5-compos.notes: the training story is the strongest thing here and it is still self-reported -- reasoning traces entered training only if their code passed the task's tests, which is a real filter, but no suite in this corpus has scored the result. its own author describes v1 as stopping after the first step, so the agentic sibling supersedes it for anything multi-step. reception is the warmest of the three additions and it is still only 6 mentions.
evidence: {community.hf-discussions} of 33 -- 6 mentions over 3 threads, none negative
no benchmark facet carried by any source
claim: execution-gated chain-of-thought distillation, with no benchmark number published for v1

zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air.one_liner: a year-old 106b that people still run because it fits, and that every newer model on this roster beats.
use_for: a 128gb box with nothing newer installed
zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air.notes: carried because the discussion tab is still busy -- 44 hf-discussions mentions over its own repo and unsloth's, mostly about what speed it gets on a strix halo -- and because a model that is measured and superseded is more useful in the table than absent from it. artificial analysis has it deprecated and every percentile it holds is in the bottom half. neither its card nor unsloth's documents a sampler set, which is why its profile reads tuned-here.

zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash.one_liner: the strongest model on this roster that a 128gb box can hold, and no released llama.cpp loads it.
avoid_for: anything local until an architecture PR merges
zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash.notes: 47 facets over four independent suites two weeks after release, which is unusual for anything this new, and they agree: {gbench.agentic}, {aa.gdpval}, arena {lmarena.rating}, terminal-bench {aa.terminalbench} and one-shot coding {gbench.oneshot} put it second on the page's default weights behind qwen3.8 flash next. the gap between that and running it is the whole story. the header declares glm5next, mainline carries no such architecture, and three separate PRs implement it -- unsloth's card names 27754, the review is happening on 27773, and the mtp head is a fourth PR behind both. the forums noticed the same thing from the other side, and the one negative reddit quote in the sample is about the PRs rather than the model. memory is tight in a way the pin does not show: UD-Q2_K_XL is 101.3 gib of weights against a 105 gib budget, so a 128k kv cache costs a rung and the page runs UD-IQ1_M instead. the vision half needs unsloth's 1.1 gib mmproj loaded beside the weights, and the three vision mentions in the corpus are questions rather than results. epoch's runs are the dissent they usually are: ale bench {epoch.ale_bench} and frontiermath tier 4 {epoch.frontiermath_tier_4_v2} against {aa.gpqa} and webdev arena {epoch.webdev_arena}.
evidence: no mainline llama.cpp release loads glm5next

zai-org/GLM-5.2.one_liner: the most-measured model in this registry and the second most-discussed, at a size whose smallest rung is 202 gib.
zai-org/GLM-5.2.notes: 67 facets across every source carried here, which makes it the best-corroborated entry in the file. the forums agree -- {community.reddit-localllama} across 42 threads, second only to the qwen3.x line -- and the people who run it keep it for the work that matters: "moved over critical, can't-fail workloads to GLM5.2" {q:6e973ffe}, and one user gave up a faster model because "glm 5.2 was giving me consistently better outputs" {q:f30099fa}. epoch's mathematics runs are the dissent: {epoch.deepswe} and otis {card.aime} against {aa.tau2} and terminal-bench hard {aa.terminalbench_hard}.
